Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
248 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Seasonable temperatures and dry conditions for Halloween. No 
hazardous weather expected through Tuesday with precipitation 
chances returning by the middle and end of next week.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Seasonable temperatures and dry conditions continue through
  Tuesday. Precipitation chances return late next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Seasonable temperatures and dry conditions continue through 
Tuesday. Precipitation chances return late next week. 

1033-1035 mb surface high pressure will build in from the north 
today before meandering over the Chesapeake Bay/Delmarva Sunday into 
Monday. As a result, expect light surface winds out of the north and 
northwest today switching to the south Sunday. Temperatures will 
remain seasonable throughout the weekend with highs in the 60s (50s 
mountains) and lows in the 40s (30s valleys).

High pressure will gradually move offshore Tuesday into Wednesday as 
a deep upper level trough approaches from the Tennessee/lower Ohio 
River Valleys. Guidance continues to show numerous pieces of 
shortwave energy expected to traverse the base of this trough during 
this period. Additionally, there is indication that a cutoff low 
will develop over the southeastern CONUS ahead of this trough 
pattern. The interaction of these systems is likely to be complex, 
with it being hard to tell exactly where all of the pieces line up 
at this stage.The GFS has at least two cutoff lows along the trough 
itself while the Canadian and Euro have a low along the trough and 
off the coastal Carolinas. As for timing, the GFS and Canadian are 
slower compared to the Euro counterpart. With that said, expect dry 
conditions to continue through Wednesday as high pressure retreats 
further offshore allowing the ridge to flatten/mid-level dry air to 
erode. This will allow precipitation chances to increase from the 
southwest late Wednesday with widespread rainfall Thursday into 
Friday. High pressure will quickly return behind the system Friday 
into the upcoming weekend before a more potent trough/push of cold 
air follows beyond the period. 

Monday through Thursday: High temperatures will be in the upper 60s 
to low 70s east of the Blue Ridge with those along and west in the 
upper 50s to 60s. Overnight low temperatures will be in the 50s each 
night.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected through at least Tuesday. 
High pressure will build from the north today before meandering over 
the area Sunday into Monday and pushing offshore by the middle of 
next week. Winds will be light and variable out of the north today 
before switching to the south Sunday and southeast Monday at less 
than 10 kts. Some patchy fog or frost is possible in the river 
valleys over the next few mornings with ground fog at the local
corridor terminals prior to daybreak each morning. Confidence 
in this is low given ample dry air in place across the region. 
However, some low chances of sub-VFR ceilings exist late Monday 
night into Tuesday depending on how the weather pattern evolves.

Sub-VFR conditions may return as early as Wednesday as rain chances 
return to the forecast. More widespread sub-VFR conditions are 
expected THursday into Friday as a wave of low pressure crosses the 
area. 

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions (north/northwest gusts 20-25 kts) are expected 
through early this morning, especially over the open waters. This is 
largely due in part to northerly channeling. Winds diminish below 
below sub-SCA levels this afternoon. Sub-SCA conditions look to 
continue Sunday into Monday with wedging high pressure meandering 
nearby. Winds will change to the south and southeast as high 
pressure sits north and east of the area. Speeds will generally be 
between 5-10 kts.

Winds turn out of the east Tuesday into Wednesday ahead of an 
approaching low pressure system, but should remain short of SCA 
criteria until at least Wednesday evening. Thereafter, winds do pick 
up slightly and could reach criteria Wednesday night. 

&&
